{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that being the 'weak link' on a team with an Internet partner would increase exercise duration compared to exercising alone, and that verbal encouragement from the partner would further increase exercise duration.",
  "design": "mixed, 3 (condition: individual control, partner with-encouragement, partner-without-encouragement) x 2 (performance block: Block 1 & Block 2) factorial design.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were assigned to exercise alone or with a virtual partner (confederate). In partner conditions, participants were told they were the 'weak link' on a team. In the encouragement condition, participants received prerecorded verbal encouragement from the partner during the second block of exercise.",
  "outcome_measure": "Total duration (in seconds) of an abdominal plank exercise held across five exercises in two blocks.",
  "population_and_setting": "College students recruited from introductory psychology and kinesiology courses at a large Midwestern university, tested in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 115,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via online and face-to-face systems; participants received course credit.",
  "analysis_plan": "3 (Condition) x 2 (Sex) ANOVA on exercise duration difference scores (Block 2 - Block 1), followed by post hoc tests to compare conditions.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used a video game (EyeToy: Kinetic) to perform isometric plank exercises. Participants in partner conditions were led to believe they were interacting with a real person via an Internet video connection, though the partner was a prerecorded confederate."
}
